title: Zone of interests under the APA
shortTitle: Zone of interests under the APA
summary: A plaintiff seeking APA review must assert an interest arguably protected or regulated by the relevant statute; economic injury alone does not answer that statutory question.
notes:
The zone-of-interests inquiry asks whether the interest the plaintiff seeks to protect falls within the interests of the statutory provision invoked. ADAPSO formulates the test alongside injury in fact. NCUA applies it generously: the plaintiff need not show that Congress specifically intended to benefit that particular plaintiff, but there must be a supported relationship between the statute’s protected interests and the interest harmed. The banking competitors qualified because the common-bond limitation constrained the customer markets credit unions could serve.

The level of generality matters. NCUA’s dissent argues that describing the interest as limiting markets converts any incidental competitive benefit into statutory protection. Air Courier illustrates a limiting result: protecting postal revenues and public postal service did not place employees’ job interests within the relevant monopoly statute. The source also cautions against assembling unrelated statutory provisions into a broad subject area to evade the test.

The later notes apply the inquiry in different settings. Thompson treats targeted retaliation against an employee as within Title VII’s protective purposes. Patchak treats neighboring land-use interests as within a statute governing federal land acquisition for tribes. Twin Rivers requires an indirect claimant’s interest to align systematically with the statutory beneficiaries and rejects paper manufacturers’ challenge to electronic disclosure. The assigned cases use historical terminology such as prudential standing.
